# EnterpriseGlue v0.38.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.37.0`.

## Highlights

- **runtime-dependencies:** Update the backend runtime to Node.js 24.22.3 and the managed-shard bootstrap runtime to Node.js 26.13.1 to fix CVE-2026-123863, a denial of service caused by improper HTTP/2 session teardown.
- **frontend-deployment:** Adds verified HTTPS and optional client certificate authentication to the frontend NGINX connection to a deployment-provided backend gateway.
- **sso:** Enable OIDC and SAML sign-in when the browser uses a separate public EnterpriseGlue API origin.

## User and administrator impact

- No behavior change. The backend keeps the Node.js 24 major, the bootstrap keeps the Node.js 26 major, and both keep their existing configuration.
- Operators can secure same-origin API traffic between the bundled frontend proxy and their backend gateway.
- Company sign-in, invitation enrollment, and OIDC account linking can start on the configured browser API origin.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Deploy the new backend image. No configuration or data changes are needed.
- Use a compatible frontend image and deployment manifests. The default upstream scheme is HTTP.
- For a split deployment, deploy the updated frontend and backend, then align the browser API origin, saved provider callback, and identity-provider registration before enabling SSO enforcement.

## API and integration compatibility

- SSO start and callback redirects are non-cacheable. OpenAPI now documents the existing global and tenant OIDC form-post callbacks.

## Configuration

- No new runtime configuration is required.
- Set API_UPSTREAM_SCHEME=https, point API_UPSTREAM at the TLS endpoint, and configure optional trust and client certificate file paths.
- Set EG_PUBLIC_API_ORIGIN on the backend to permit canonical sign-in callbacks on one additional exact origin.

## Database migrations

- Migration inventories and schema-plan identities remain unchanged.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- Pin the Wolfi backend runtime to nodejs-24 24.22.3-r2 and the managed-shard bootstrap runtime to nodejs-26 26.13.1-r1, both of which contain the fix for CVE-2026-123863 (HIGH).
- HTTPS verifies the upstream certificate chain and hostname. mTLS uses deployment-mounted client credentials and requires upstream enforcement.
- Production callbacks require HTTPS. Canonical paths, tenant bindings, and host-only sign-in and session cookies are retained.

## Known limitations

- The deployment provides the TLS termination endpoint and owns the final hop to the HTTP backend.
- Split-origin sign-in requires same-site browser API access and a trusted shared XSRF cookie domain when the hostnames differ.
- SAML single logout and frontend plugin assets retain their existing routing requirements.

## Rollback

- Restore the previous image only after independently checking its current security acceptance.
- Restore the previous upstream address and network access before rolling the frontend workloads. Clear TLS-only settings when restoring HTTP.
- Restore the previous frontend settings, saved provider callback and identity-provider registration before removing EG_PUBLIC_API_ORIGIN or reverting the backend.

## Validation evidence

- Dependency-security override and managed-shard bootstrap tests, both runtime image builds and exact-image vulnerability scans.
- Exercise HTTP, verified HTTPS, mTLS, certificate rejection, and independent frontend liveness in the container proxy. Render supported deployment manifests.
- Exercise split-origin browser navigation, OIDC and SAML sign-in, bundle preview, same-origin compatibility, and rejected callback URLs.
- Compare registered sign-in routes with generated OpenAPI, including redirect headers and callback parameters.
